reviewMethod: Rendered state sheets reviewed at reduced player size for landscape and phone-like width for Shorts. Verdicts compare communication, hierarchy, typography, motion, rhythm, consistency, and format adaptation rather than schema validity.

goldens.whatWorks: NOW versus LATER reads immediately; both options exist at frame 0; the baseline and restrained accent make the tradeoff legible.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The two fields remain highly symmetrical and the VS marker is conventional.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: On a premium pass, replace VS with a named delay axis and make the value shift more explicit.

goldens.whatWorks: The stack is genuinely vertical, large at phone size, and leaves captions and the interaction rail clear.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The paired horizontal rules still expose a reusable comparison grammar.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Add a subtle temporal arrow between NOW and LATER if the surrounding edit can support it.

goldens.whatWorks: The semantic distinction is understood without reading the narration caption; unequal copy remains balanced.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The central divider is familiar and the supporting descriptions are visually quiet.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Directly encode predefined flow versus adaptive loop in a future specialized grammar.

goldens.whatWorks: Labels remain comfortably readable and the mobile hierarchy clearly moves from traditional software to agent.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The stacked fields share the same structure as other comparisons.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Use a small deterministic/agentic behavior glyph only if the video's icon language already supports it.

goldens.whatWorks: The numeric delta is dominant, the conclusion is visible, and the solved version is clearer than the legacy columns.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: Equal field treatment is slightly generic for a financial comparison.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Add a shared compounding baseline when real time-horizon data is available.

goldens.whatWorks: Large fee values survive phone-size review and the key difference stays above captions.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The vertical stack is intentionally reusable rather than topic-specific.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Use a small accumulating-cost indicator if it can be evidence-backed.

goldens.whatWorks: Before/after direction is clear, restrained, and more editorial than card UI.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The fields are visually similar despite different strategic behavior.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Introduce directional movement only at the narration pivot, not continuously.

goldens.whatWorks: The frame uses the vertical canvas deliberately and the learning-speed takeaway is the final focal point.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The comparison rails are visibly part of a system.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Increase the separation between old and new with a semantic arrow in a topic-specific pass.

goldens.whatWorks: The falling curve tells the story before labels are read; the annotation and takeaway reinforce rather than compete.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The annotation leader is mechanically straight.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Use a hand-tuned elbow leader if this becomes a hero chart.

goldens.whatWorks: The plot remains large, the line is readable at phone width, and the draw reveals the trend progressively.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: Axis typography is utilitarian rather than bespoke.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Drop one more nonessential tick for very small embedded players.

goldens.whatWorks: Enterprise is dominant through height, accent, direct value, and takeaway; every label need not be inspected.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The basic vertical-bar grammar is intentionally conventional.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: No change unless real brand or source styling is supplied.

goldens.whatWorks: Horizontal recomposition is materially better than a shrunken desktop chart; values and categories pass phone-size review.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The axis and direct labels use a general-purpose editorial system.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Tighten category-to-bar spacing slightly for a final branded pass.

goldens.whatWorks: The two lines are distinguishable, directly labeled, and the widening gap is immediately apparent.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Add a shaded delta only if it remains subordinate to the primary line.

goldens.whatWorks: The trend and gap remain legible at phone width without a detached legend.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: Direct endpoint labels are compact and somewhat mechanical.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Hand-place the secondary endpoint label if the values converge in real data.

goldens.whatWorks: The highlighted multi-step point and takeaway make the conclusion obvious before axis inspection.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The dot plot is sparse by design and could feel neutral in a hero slot.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Add a reference threshold only when it has real semantic meaning.

goldens.whatWorks: Dots and values remain readable at reduced phone width and the plot does not collapse into a tiny desktop chart.
goldens.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: Category labels use the same axis treatment as other charts.
goldens.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Shorten category labels further if production data is longer.

regressions.whatWorks: The comparison and curve share palette, title position, restraint, and caption behavior; both communicate instant-gratification semantics immediately.
regressions.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The transition evidence is a state sheet rather than a fully graded final edit.
regressions.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Use a clean cut at the conceptual shift and preserve the blue accent across it.

regressions.whatWorks: Wide-frame utilization and hierarchy are consistent between comparison and chart; the chart is materially clearer than legacy.
regressions.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: Both scenes use the same top-title system, which is consistent but recognizable.
regressions.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: Vary title alignment only when an adjacent shot provides a strong match anchor.

regressions.whatWorks: Both scenes are truly recomposed, readable at phone width, caption-safe, and free of a right-rail collision.
regressions.whatStillLooksGeneratedOrTemplated: The reusable rule language remains visible.
regressions.whatWouldAHumanEditorChange: No structural change; apply final brand typography if available.

legacyComparisons.verdict: Solved is materially better in frame-0 completeness, explicit key difference, format adaptation, and controlled emphasis. Legacy has larger headline energy but weaker semantic structure.
Solved is materially better through real axes, data-derived scales, explicit takeaway, source semantics, and mobile recomposition.
